_comment: Who uses the Go code that phase 2 of ADR-036 deletes (docs/adr/036-single-parser-effective-config.md
section 11 and its implementation map; #2766, #2486). Phase 2 may delete a package or a vendored
yaml.v3 patch only once its users below are gone or rewritten. ADR-036 step 3 (#2905) deleted
pkg/pyyamlcompat, pkg/routingpolicy, the judging part of pkg/receiverspec and the spaces-only patch;
a deleted package stays here as a row with no importers, so a new import of it is red.
from the source of BOTH Go modules (components/threshold-exporter/app, components/tenant-api)
with go/parser and goes red when they differ from this file in either direction.
Package level, not per symbol (owner decision on #2766, 2026-10-10): what stays inside a package
importers: one row per (repo-relative directory, whether the importing file is a _test.go file);
every .go file counts whatever its build tags, external `_test` packages included; not read:
the module root's third_party/ (a third_party/ deeper down is read) and testdata/ at any depth.
patches: exactly the third_party/*.patch files on disk, the same set
Dispositions: package delete | split | deleted (the directory is gone and nothing imports it);
patch keep | delete-when-unrelied (believed_reliant: exporter-module directories, which must exist).

packages.category: ADR-036 section 11: Go code imitating how Python (PyYAML) reads YAML
packages.notes: Deleted in ADR-036 step 3 (#2905). It decoded a yaml.v3 node into the value PyYAML's SafeLoader builds; with the generator the only judge of routing and policy nothing needs it. A file the generator refuses for a key PyYAML counts twice is named by parse-tree (duplicate_key), not by a Go copy of the rule.

packages.category: Not a row of ADR-036 section 11: the Go copy of the generator's receiver rules, whose judging callers ADR-036 removes (#2899)
packages.notes: Split done in ADR-036 step 3 (#2905): the judging part (Check and the per-type field rules) is deleted; Known stays for the exporter (pkg/config looks a receiver type up; it does not judge).

packages.category: ADR-036 section 11: Go code imitating how Python reads YAML, mixed with small helpers unrelated to parsing
packages.notes: Deleted in ADR-036 step 3 (#2905): the PyYAML emulation (shapeWork, pyResolve, ParseDomainPolicies, UnmarshalPolicy, the policyDecoder that turned SpacesOnly on) and the Go routing and policy judgement da-guard ran. The helpers that do not parse had moved before (#2899): IsValidTenantID (callers use pkg/tenantid), LevelOf and IsDomainPolicyFile (internal/confdlayout); the routing-profiles file names are cmd/da-guard's routingProfilesNames. IsDisabled had no caller left once da-guard stopped judging routing (#2904).

patches.reason: Always on (decode.go keeps Tag "!" on a non-plain scalar), so no call site shows who depends on it. The exporter relies on it (ADR-036 section 7: isMergeKey in config_file.go takes a `! "<<"` key as a merge, validateSloObjective in custom_alert.go refuses `! "99.9"`); it is deleted in ADR-036 step 4 together with the generator's switch to parse-tree. NOT mechanically proven: removing an import does not prove the behaviour unused.

Upstream's own fix (go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.2+, #2913): a merge beside a non-scalar key is a decode error, not a process-ending panic. Every typed decode of a tenant or config file depends on it, independent of the PyYAML emulation; it goes only when the vendored copy is replaced by an upstream release that carries it.
Linear duplicate-key detection for large mappings; the exporter's own config decoding uses it for performance, independent of the PyYAML emulation.
